name: Ringo SP-2 'Buzzkill'
description:
A compact stun pistol the size of a derringer, designed as a concealed personal defense weapon for civilians and corporate employees in GLMZ's mid-tier districts. The SP-2 fires a single capacitor-driven arc across two exposed electrodes at the weapon's muzzle, delivering a contact-range shock powerful enough to cause involuntary muscle spasm and disorientation for 3-5 seconds. The weapon must be physically pressed against the target to discharge, giving it effectively zero range but making it nearly impossible to detect in a pocket or handbag.

Ringo markets the Buzzkill as a personal safety device — 'your last line of defense' — and sells it in a range of colors and finishes targeted at the corporate professional demographic. The weapon has become a fashion accessory as much as a tool, with designer versions available from Ringo's lifestyle division. The normalization of carrying a concealed electrical weapon has had predictable consequences: assault-with-Buzzkill incidents in GLMZ's nightlife districts have increased 300% since the weapon's introduction, and 'getting buzzed' has become a common experience in clubs, bars, and crowded transit.
specifications:
range: Contact only
discharge: 25,000 volts, single pulse
incapacitation: 3-5 seconds disorientation
charges: 15 per power cell
weight: 0.1 kg
length: 80mm
form factor: Derringer-sized, pocket concealment
tactical_use: Last-resort personal defense at contact range. Users press the weapon against an attacker and fire, using the momentary incapacitation to create distance and escape. Not designed for sustained combat or repeated application.
cultural_context: The Buzzkill has become ubiquitous in GLMZ's middle tiers — carried by office workers, retail employees, students, and anyone else who can afford Φ120 for a sense of security. Its prevalence has created a new social dynamic where physical contact with strangers carries a risk of electrical assault, contributing to the city's culture of personal space enforcement through technology.
story_hooks: A modified Buzzkill has killed someone — a Φ120 personal safety device with an aftermarket capacitor that delivers a lethal discharge. The modification costs Φ30 and takes ten minutes. Instructions are circulating on underground networks.

Ringo's sales data for Buzzkill units has been cross-referenced with assault reports, revealing that the districts with the highest Buzzkill sales also have the highest assault rates. The weapon designed to prevent violence is enabling it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A diminutive, almost delicate stun pistol that resembles a compact derringer or vintage pocket revolver. The Buzzkill trades intimidation for subtlety—it's designed to vanish into a jacket pocket or evening clutch rather than command attention. The silhouette is slightly bulbous at the grip, tapering toward a deliberately thin muzzle crowned with two exposed electrode contacts that gleam like watchful eyes.
physical_description.dimensions: 80mm length, 35mm width at grip, 25mm depth. Muzzle electrode spacing: 12mm apart
physical_description.weight_description: Featherlight and almost inconsequential in hand—100 grams distributed to sit perfectly in a closed fist. Feels more like a luxury pen than a weapon, with no hint of heft or menace
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer chassis with reinforced grip sections. Muzzle assembly is brushed steel with integrated copper contact points
physical_description.finish: High-gloss or matte polymer body (varies by color variant). Brushed satin steel at electrode housing. Optional chrome or titanium accents on designer editions
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in corporate neutrals (matte black, pearl white, gunmetal gray) and lifestyle colors (rose gold, sapphire blue, obsidian). Electrodes are always burnished copper or silver
physical_description.grip_texture: Soft-touch rubberized polymer, slightly tacky, with subtle diamond knurling. Designer editions feature wrapped synthetic leather or textured composite grips
distinctive_features: Twin exposed electrode contacts at muzzle—the only overtly 'weapon' element of the design
Minimalist charging port recessed beneath grip (micro-connector)
Subtle LED power indicator (blue when charged, amber when depleted) embedded in grip
Contact-activation safety: small raised button must be pressed against target skin to complete circuit
Serial number and 'RingoMart Personal Safety Systems' logo laser-etched on grip
Deliberately rounded, organic form factor—almost ergonomic to the point of appearing medical or therapeutic
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: RingoMart logo (stylized 'R' in a circle) screen-printed on lower grip. Small serial plate on left side with date code. Safety warnings in microfont along the slide. Designer editions may have custom engravings or initials
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually pristine or near-perfect—these are lifestyle accessories kept in designer cases. Well-maintained owners keep electrodes polished. Heavy use shows minor scuffing on grip, slightly dulled electrode contacts, and visible wear on safety button. Abused units may have cracked polymer, corroded electrodes, or separation in the grip panels
